summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results vs VeraHealth's baseline provider. Redwood SE presented detailed latency and throughput numbers; main wins were lower p95/p99 and higher sustained throughput using Redwood Dedicated with batching + KV caching. Customer raised questions about tail latency variability, quantization impact on quality, and networking/egress in their VPC. Agreed next steps: share benchmark scripts, run a high-concurrency p99 test in VeraHealth staging, and follow up with pricing + security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood CSM), Liam (VeraHealth CTO), Priya (Lead ML Eng), Carlos (DevOps), Maya (PM)

[00:00] Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick check — audio good?
[00:06] Liam (VeraHealth): Yep, loud and clear. Thanks.
[00:10] Samira (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll share my screen, we have the week-over-week benchmark deck and the raw numbers from the instrumented runs. We'll try to keep it tight, call it 30 minutes of content and then Q&A.
[00:22] Priya (VeraHealth): Sounds good. We're mostly interested in p99 under load and the impact of int8 quantization on answer quality.
[00:30] Samira: Great — that's on the agenda. Quick reminder on methodology: runs were in us-west-2, same instance size on baseline provider and Redwood Dedicated where possible; request distribution matches your production prompt mix (short chat traffic ~ 65%, long-generations ~ 35%). We ran both streaming and non-streaming flows. There's some minor tran-scription — sorry, typo in the deck — but numbers are accurate.
[01:05] Samira: Starting with latency: baseline provider p50/p95/p99 for the long-gen workload was 120ms / 420ms / 890ms. On Redwood Dedicated with batching and KV prefix cache we saw 95ms / 330ms / 720ms. That's approximately 18% reduction at p99 and ~22% at p95.
[01:40] Priya: Okay that's promising, how consistent were those p99s across runs? We saw some spikes on the baseline during the afternoon window.
[01:50] Samira: We observed higher tail variance on baseline; their host-level autoscaler causes rebalancing which adds tail. Our Dedicated pool keeps warmed KV caches and continuous batching which smooths those spikes. I will note — our p99 still had occasional 1.2s outliers when a cold eviction happened during the long-gen test.
[02:20] Carlos: Are those cold evictions because of memory pressure on your side or due to model swapping?
[02:28] Samira: Usually model swapping when we scale down. We recommended pinning the model for a steady-state Dedicated pool; for the POC we had a small burst policy — that caused a few evictions.
[02:40] Ethan: Also worth noting we ran an int8 quantized config for one of the tests — that changed the numbers a bit.
[02:48] Priya: Right — what's the impact on throughput and latency when using int8?
[02:52] Samira: With int8+quant compression we saw ~1.6x throughput increase and p99 came down to ~540ms for long-gen in the quantized run. But as expected there's quality delta: we evaluated 150 prompts from your eval set — automated metrics stayed within 2.5% of baseline for summary-style prompts, but for the few hallucination-sensitive ones manual review flagged subtle rank ordering shifts.
[03:32] Maya (PM): That's the key — we can accept small metric drift for cost, but not for critical clinical summaries.
[03:40] Samira: Agreed. For those flows we recommend FP16 or mixed precision and selective quantization on non-sensitive models.
[03:48] [04:00] Samira: Throughput numbers: baseline sustained tokens/sec for the mixed workload was ~14k t/s; Redwood Dedicated sustained ~25k t/s under same concurrency with optimized batching and kernel selection. Peak bursts hit ~37k t/s on Redwood with continuous batching enabled.
[04:30] Liam: 25k vs 14k, that's a big delta. Can you remind us of the GPU config used?
[04:36] Samira: Sure — baseline used 2x V100-equivalent (their managed offering). Our Dedicated run used 4x A100-ish class GPUs with optimized kernels. Config details in the repo — I'll share.
[04:52] Priya: How much of the improvement is just more GPUs vs runtime improvements? If we tried Redwood with similar GPU count on the baseline provider would we see the same?
[05:00] Samira: Good question — we did a micro-comparison: same nominal GPU count, Redwood runtime delivered ~1.25x better tokens/sec due to improved kernel selection and batching. The rest of the delta is from total GPU count and memory (KV cache) advantages. So both matter.
[05:25] Ethan: I'll add that the smart routing + fallback we demoed last week wasn't enabled in these runs; enabling it adds resilience but can add a few ms tail in cross-region fallback scenarios.
[05:40] [06:00] Liam: Network — we need to confirm egress and VPC peering. Carlos, do we have any limits in staging that would affect throughput?
[06:06] Carlos: Our staging has a 10Gbps egress cap to the cloud region; if you're pushing 37k t/s that might saturate. We need the raw bytes/sec numbers to check.
[06:18] Samira: We'll include bytes/sec in the artifact. For reference, 25k t/s roughly split across short streaming vs long tokens is about 2.2Gbps in our setup (depends on tokenization).
[06:36] Priya: Okay that's within our 10Gbps but if spikes hit peak we might see network burst.
[06:43] [07:00] Samira: On batching: we tuned batch windows to 20–60ms depending on the route. That gave us good latency/throughput tradeoff; longer windows increase throughput but hurt p50. Your production SLOs are p95 < 400ms so we tuned toward that.
[07:20] Priya: For the streaming flows — how does that change?
[07:24] Samira: Streaming reduces end-to-end time for user perceived latency but can increase server-side ops; we saw effective p95 improvement for short chat when using streaming.
[07:35] [08:00] Ethan: Wanted to call out cost: for the config tested (4-GPU Dedicated), estimated per-month unit cost we provided in the deck — roughly 45% cheaper per effective token vs their managed baseline when accounting for better batching and cache hit rates. Exact numbers in the pricing sheet.
[08:22] Liam: That's compelling. We'll need the exact math — how you amortize GPU-hours against throughput.
[08:28] Ethan: We'll send the breakdown; Samira will include the runbook and raw logs so you can validate the math.
[08:36] [09:00] Priya: On the quality side: can you share the eval set results and the samples where int8 drifted? We want to triage which prompts are sensitive.
[09:08] Samira: Yes — we'll attach the 150-prompt eval CSV and a small manual sample set flagged for review. We anonymized patient PHI per your request.
[09:20] Maya: For compliance we need to see encryption at rest and KMS usage. Is that part of the POC for Dedicated?
[09:28] Ethan: Yes, Dedicated supports customer KMS integration and we can show the audit logs. We'll route you to our security docs and schedule a SecOps call.
[09:40] [10:00] Carlos: About deployment — if we go Private (VPC) later, will the same benchmark improvements translate? Latency wise I'd prefer to compare Private vs Dedicated.
[10:08] Samira: The Private runtime is the same core engine, but network topology and your on-prem hardware will determine absolute numbers. We usually see similar per-GPU performance; latency differences come from network hops. For the POC we can spin a Private pilot if you want a direct apples-to-apples.
[10:28] Priya: That would be ideal but it's heavier lift. For next steps maybe run the high-concurrency p99 on baseline + Redwood, then we decide.
[10:38] [11:00] Samira: Quick note on stability: we instrumented for cold start, memory pressure, and kernel fallback. The rare 1.2s outliers correlated with model swapping and one node reboot during a provider maintenance window; we flagged those in the logs.
[11:14] Liam: Maintenance windows — baseline had scheduled maintenance during one run?
[11:18] Samira: Yes, minor timing overlap with their host autoscaler. We excluded the worst run from averages but left the spikes visible in the artifact.
[11:30] [12:00] Ethan: Okay let's do a short demo of the dashboard so you can see per-token latency and cache hits live.
[12:10] Samira: Sharing screen — here's the per-route view, p50/p95/p99 lines, and a cache hit rate chart. For this POC your overall prefix cache hit was ~42% which reduced token generation work significantly.
[12:40] Priya: 42% — can we tune that higher? Most of our prompts have a structured prefix so I expect more cacheable content.
[12:48] Samira: Yes, you can increase hit rate by identifying canonical prefixes and using explicit caching headers; our analyzer suggests potentially pushing to ~60% with minimal prompt changes. We'll highlight the top 10 prefixes in the repo.
[13:10] [14:00] Maya: Any legal/procurement blockers we're expecting if we move to Dedicated?
[14:06] Ethan: Standard enterprise terms, SOC 2 attestation, SAML SSO, and support SLAs. For Private we can add additional compliance packages. We'll share the contract template.
[14:24] [15:00] Priya: A small nit — in the raw logs I saw a few transcribed model names like "CloudModelX" spelled different; was that the baseline vendor?
[15:10] Samira: Yeah baseline labelled as CloudModex in one log — transcription and vendor naming is messy, apologies.
[15:18] [16:00] Liam: Ok let's recap next steps quickly.
[16:06] Ethan: Recap — Redwood shares benchmark repo + README and bytes/sec details (Samira) by 8/13. Redwood shares Dedicated pricing (Ethan) by 8/14. VeraHealth runs 1k-concurrency p99 test in staging and shares logs (Priya) by 8/18. Security follow-up scheduled for week of 8/17.
[16:36] Priya: We'll prioritize the 1k-concurrency run; Carlos will confirm staging region and egress.
[16:44] Carlos: Yep I'll follow up.
[16:48] [17:00] Samira: Any final Qs on QoL or observable metrics?
[17:04] Priya: Can you also include CPU/GPU utilization and kernel fallback traces in the artifact? That helps us correlate slowdowns.
[17:12] Samira: Yes will include util% and fallback events.
[17:18] Maya: For the eval, can you mark the examples where manual review flagged hallucination risk?
[17:22] Samira: Will do, we'll separate them into a 'sensitive' bucket.
[17:28] [18:00] Ethan: All right thanks team — we'll send the artifacts and pricing after the call. Want to tentatively meet next Monday same time to review VeraHealth's 1k tests?
[18:38] Liam: Works for us.
[18:42] [19:00] Jules (Redwood CSM): I'll schedule and include SecOps invite.
[19:06] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[19:10] [42:00] End of call

References & artifacts mentioned: benchmark repo link (shared post-call), pricing sheet (Redwood Dedicated config), 150-prompt eval CSV, cache prefix analyzer CSV, security docs link (SOC2/KMS).
